records.title: Quantum-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Ubiquitous LLM Inference via Embodied UAV Swarms
records.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

identity_evidence.quote: Quantum-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Ubiquitous LLM Inference via Embodied UAV Swarms

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 14-page peer-reviewed IEEE journal article presenting original system modeling, Dec-POMDP formulation, Q-MAA2C algorithm, and simulation evaluation.
primary_full_report.quote: To address this challenge, this paper studies an edge inference system assisted by an embodied UAV agent swarm, where UAVs actively sense user mobility and neighboring UAV states to make local decisions on trajectory control, user association, and inference-request routing.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Both simulation topologies evaluate a fleet of two decentralized rotary-wing UAVs (U = 2) coordinating trajectories, user association, and request routing.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: In both scenarios, two rotary-wing UAVs, i.e., U = 2, deploy from [0, 500] and [500, 500] m at a constant altitude H = 100 m.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Embodied UAVs jointly orchestrate user association and cache-aware LLM inference-request routing across a ground-user, multi-UAV, and KV-cache edge-server hierarchy for two-phase prefill and decoding.
collaborative_inference.quote: The GU uploads input tokens to the selected ES through the associated UAV, and the ES performs prefill using the new input and the uncached historical context.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Evaluates Q-MAA2C via TensorFlow Quantum and Cirq simulations across two multi-ES, multi-GU, 2-UAV scenarios against classical/non-entangled MARL variants and decoupled baselines.
evaluative_evidence.quote: Simulations are implemented using TensorFlow Quantum and Cirq, following the models in Section III.

date_window.rationale: Published online 23 July 2026 (current version 6 August 2026, Vol. 12, 2026), within the 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25 window.
date_window.quote: Date of publication 23 July 2026; date of current version 6 August 2026.

english.rationale: Full text is written in English.
english.quote: 6G mobile edge networks are emerging as a key infrastructure for ubiquitous large language model (LLM) inference services.

alignment.rationale: Jointly optimizes multi-UAV trajectories, user association, cache-aware LLM inference-request routing to edge servers, and active sensing scheduling.
alignment.quote: Building on the above observations, this paper studies cache-aware edge LLM inference assisted by an embodied UAV agent swarm and develops a hybrid quantum-classical MARL solution for decentralized UAV-swarm control.

records.title: SwarmChain: Collaborative LLM Inference for UAV Swarm Control

identity_evidence.quote: SwarmChain: Collaborative LLM Inference for UAV Swarm Control

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 8-page peer-reviewed IEEE magazine article presenting the CoLLM-Also distributed LLM inference system, SwarmChain control pipeline, and hardware/simulation experiments.
primary_full_report.quote: To address these issues, we develop SwarmChain, a collaborative LLM inference system for UAV swarm control. We first design a tensor parallelism based collaborative reasoning framework (CoLLM) to enable multi-device collaboration for distributing computational loads.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Evaluates multi-device collaborative inference (up to 5 SBCs and 10-50 simulated nodes) integrated with multi-UAV swarm formation and spacing control in AirSim.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: Based on the observed results, the system is capable of handling various commands, accurately controlling the UAV swarm, and executing the corresponding control behaviors.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Partitions decoder-only LLM weights via tensor parallelism (CoLLM) across a host and worker drone nodes with resource-aware adaptive load scheduling (Also) and KV caching over MPI.
collaborative_inference.quote: In a swarm consisting of one host node and N worker nodes (drones), the limited computational resources of individual drones necessitate distributing the computational load across multiple drones. By employing tensor parallelism, model tensors are partitioned and allocated to worker nodes for parallel computation.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Reports benchtop experiments on Raspberry Pi-4B, OrangePi AIpro(20T), and Jetson Xavier NX running quantized StableLM-3B-4E1T and Llama2 7B/13B, plus simulated heterogeneous load scheduling, node-loss restarts, and AirSim swarm control.
evaluative_evidence.quote: Considering that Raspberry Pi is a common example of resource-constrained devices, the experiments are conducted first on multiple Raspberry Pi devices and then on heterogeneous platforms: Orange Pi AI Pro (20T) and NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX, as shown in the Fig. 4(a).

date_window.rationale: Published online 6 June 2025 (current version 30 September 2025, September 2025 issue), within the 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25 window.

english.rationale: Full text is written in English.
english.quote: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms have the potential to perform sophisticated collaborative tasks. However, efficiently managing UAV swarms in harsh environments without ground command centers remains a significant challenge.

records.primary_reason: All six eligibility gates PASS: primary_full_report (YES), multi_uav_evaluated (YES), collaborative_inference (YES), evaluative_evidence (YES), date_window (YES), and english (YES).

alignment.rationale: Partitions LLM attention and MLP weight matrices via tensor parallelism (CoLLM) and adaptively schedules weight index intervals across heterogeneous drone nodes (Also), including node-loss task restarts.
alignment.quote: By designing a general framework capable of running decode-only structured LLMs, CoLLM partitions and deploys LLMs across distributed devices, enabling collaborative inference among resource-constrained and heterogeneous devices.

records.title: RDI-LLM: A Resilient Distributed Inference Framework for LLMs in Resource-Constrained UAV Swarm

identity_evidence.quote: RDI-LLM: A Resilient Distributed Inference Framework for LLMs in Resource-Constrained UAV Swarm

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 16-page peer-reviewed journal article accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology (IEEE Xplore Early Access accepted author manuscript).
primary_full_report.quote: This article has been accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology. This is the author's version which has not been fully edited and content may change prior to final publication. Citation information: DOI 10.1109/TVT.2026.3755123

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Evaluates self-organized UAV swarms scaling from 8 to 32 UAVs (default N = 16 UAVs) across interference, bandwidth, and mobility sweeps.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: Fig. 7(b) evaluates scaling from 8 to 32 UAVs. Increasing the swarm size provides more replicas but also increases co-channel contention.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Partitions decoder-only LLM FFN layers into disjoint shards placed redundantly across UAVs, with an elected leader UAV orchestrating Sufficient-is-Enough partial activation and first-successful aggregation.
collaborative_inference.quote: RDI-LLM avoids this execution barrier by partitioning the FFN of decoder-only LLMs into fine-grained shards, deploying redundant replicas across UAVs, and activating only a sufficient replica subset during inference. Each layer advances after the first valid result for every required shard

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Discrete-event simulations on decomposed Llama-2-13B and Llama-2-70B workloads compare RDI-LLM against eight baselines plus ablations, sensitivity sweeps, and channel/mobility stress tests.
evaluative_evidence.quote: We implement a discrete-event simulator with an offline placement phase and an online inference phase. The simulator supports decomposed Llama-2-13B and Llama-2-70B models in FP16; the results reported in Figs. 5–11 and Tables IV–V use Llama-2-70B.

multi_uav_evaluated.quote: We classify an observed four-UAV tuple as same-depth only when all four UAVs choose the same exit; all other tuples are mixed-depth.

records.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Task Offloading With Collaborative Inference in UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing Networks

primary_full_report.quote: To address these challenges, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based DNN Partitioning and Dynamic Trajectory Selection (DPDTS) method, which reduces end-to-end latency and system energy consumption through task offloading and collaborative inference.

multi_uav_evaluated.quote: Fig. 8 shows the flight trajectories obtained by DPDTS in four test scenarios, where the four colored rings represent the flight paths of the four UAVs, the stars are randomly generated initial positions at the edges, and the triangles represent the GUs.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Partitions ground-user DNN inference tasks (ResNet-34, VGG-16, AlexNet) layer-by-layer between local devices and matched UAV edge servers alongside joint compute allocation and multi-UAV trajectory control.
collaborative_inference.quote: The first half of each task of the ith GU is executed locally, while the second half of each task of the ith GU is offloaded to the UAV for execution.

records.title: Secure Split Offloading and Trajectory Design for UAV-Assisted Multi-Exit Collaborative DNN Inference

identity_evidence.quote: Secure Split Offloading and Trajectory Design for UAV-Assisted Multi-Exit Collaborative DNN Inference

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 16-page peer-reviewed IEEE journal article presenting the dual-UAV multi-exit collaborative inference and cooperative jamming formulation, alternating optimization algorithm, and simulation evaluation.
primary_full_report.quote: To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel UAV-assisted CI framework via multi-exit DNNs and cooperative jamming.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Models and simulates a dual-UAV system comprising one UAV edge server and one friendly cooperative UAV jammer with inter-UAV synchronization, collision avoidance, and coupled trajectory optimization.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: In this section, we perform simulations to validate the effectiveness of our proposed UAV-assisted CI scheme. We consider that a UAV server and a UAV jammer are deployed within an area of 800×800 m2 to provide CI.

collaborative_inference.quote: device k executes the initial layers from 0 to mk[n] and the UAV server handles the remaining layers from mk[n]+1 to Msk[n].

evaluative_evidence.quote: Moreover, we train a multi-exit ResNet-18 model on the CIFAR-10 dataset. As shown in Fig. 2, the adopted model consists of a ResNet-18 backbone with an initial convolution layer, a max-pooling layer, and eight residual blocks.
